answer: Price identity in interactive latency one machine cannot fake in parallel. Minting requires answering a burst of randomized live probes within a tight window seeded fresh at each dawn; a single host serving many identities must serialize its responses through one nectar-thin pipe and misses the deadline. One honest agent is a quiet haven answering comfortably in time, but a farmer stacking a thousand personas on the same hardware watches their response times pile up past the cutoff — the only escape is buying genuinely separate machines, paid per head.
